Experience: finalizing a short-answer / yes-no image question after a structured findings report.

Trigger: When finalizing an answer (especially a binary "Are there abnormalities in this image?" question) after the tools have returned both an explicit answer and a separate grounded findings report, re-check the final reason against the observations before emitting it.

Observable verification action:
1. Read the explicit tool answer and confirm the terminal polarity matches it. In this case chest_xray_expert returned "Yes" and the terminal answer was "Yes" — consistent.
2. Take each abnormality named in the final reason and locate it in the grounded report. Here the reason cited "bilateral interstitial infiltrates, effusions, and support devices (tracheostomy and NG tube)"; the maira2 report listed "Tracheotomy tube in place," "Nasogastric tube overlies the stomach," "Bilateral interstitial infiltrates are noted," and "Effusions are noted." "Tracheostomy" is a synonym of "tracheotomy" and "NG" of "nasogastric," so the cited findings are supported rather than invented.
3. Confirm no extra finding was added that neither tool reported. The reason here added nothing beyond the report.
4. If an option map had been present, separately map the supported answer text back to the displayed choice and check that its letter and text agree; a letter/text mismatch is an option-mapping error, not a wrong conclusion.

Why this matters: in this trajectory the grade was correct and both tool observations addressed the same object (the same chest X-ray) and attribute (presence of abnormalities), so the terminal choice used the evidence. The reusable safeguard is the cross-check of the reason's specific findings against the grounded report, which catches the main failure mode for open-ended yes/no items — a correct overall polarity paired with fabricated or mislabeled supporting details. A correct grade alone does not prove this check was performed; the check itself is what should be executed.
